newsitem.title: UK: BT Pension unit to buy stake in Argent.
newsitem.headline: BT Pension unit to buy stake in Argent.

text.p: BT Pension Scheme said on Friday its BriTel property unit had agreed to buy a 39.5 percent stake in property developer Argent Group Plc for 375p per share in cash and loan notes.
BriTel will buy the shares from Warburg, Pincus and some of Argent's directors.
After the deal, BT Pension Scheme and BriTel Property will own 24.3 million Argent shares, or about 40.2 percent of the company.
To comply with UK takeover rules, BriTel said it would offer to buy the rest of Argent in a bid of 375p per share, valuing the company at about 240 million stg.
However, BriTel said it wanted Argent to maintain its stock exchange listing.
UK takeover rules require companies owning more than 29.9 percent of a firm to make a cash offer for the rest of the company's share capital.
The offer represented a discount of 16.7 percent to Thursday's closing price of 450p per share.
BriTel said the bid was final and would not be increased.

"Despite being required for technical reasons to make an offer under the City Code, we would prefer to remain a significant shareholder providing long-term support to Argent's property activities," BriTel said.
After the deal, Argent's joint chief executives, Michael Freeman and Peter Freeman, who sold their shares in the company, would remain with the firm for 12 months. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
